title: Clicking or right-clicking an item on the timeline moves the playhead there
goal: A click on any item on the timeline (a clip, a piece, a sound, a title, a caption, a zoom bar) picks it AND moves the playhead to the moment clicked, as Premiere and Final Cut users expect. A right-click moves the playhead to the moment clicked before the menu opens, so 'at playhead' commands act where the person pointed. Right-clicking inside something already picked (one item, several, or a range) moves the playhead too, but the menu's commands act on what is picked, not just the item under the pointer.
notes:
User's words (2026-10-12): "if I click somewhere on an item in the timeline, I not only expect it to select, but I expect the playhead (the red line) to move to that location. or, if I right click on a position within an item, I expect the playhead to move there before showing options. If i have a selection and right click on it, we can move the playhead but options apply to the range of the item or items selected."

From code reading (not run): ClipPiecesBar.swift:427-449 .onTapGesture picks the clip (selectClipPiece / extendSelection) with no time and no playhead move; :450 .contextMenu is a plain SwiftUI context menu that never learns where the press was. Needs a location-aware tap (onTapGesture(coordinateSpace:) or SpatialTapGesture) mapped through the lane's ms scale, and a right-mouse-down hook (NSView rightMouseDown or a secondary-click recognizer) that scrubs before the menu is built. Same for title bars, zoom bars (ZoomLane.swift), key lanes (ClipPiecesBar.swift:1035 pickClipKey already takes atMS), caption cues. Coordinate with a-range-stays-on-top-when-you-pick-a-clip-and-it (range plus pick menus) so the two land on one right-click path.
acceptance: Reproduce first at Next defaults: click and right-click at the middle of a clip, a sound, a title bar and a zoom bar; record that the playhead does not move today

A plain click (no drag past the drag threshold) on any timeline item picks it as today and moves the playhead to the clicked time, snapped the way playhead clicks on the ruler snap; Shift or Command click still adds or removes from the pick and also moves the playhead; a press that turns into a drag (move, trim) does NOT move the playhead

Right-click on an item: the playhead moves to the clicked time first, then the menu opens; if the item was not picked it becomes picked (as macOS does for a right-click on an unselected row); 'at playhead' rows (Split Here, Add Zoom, Add Key, Freeze Frame, Add Click at Playhead and the like) act at that moment

Right-click inside the current pick (one or several picked items, or inside a held range per a-range-stays-on-top-when-you-pick-a-clip-and-it): the playhead moves, the pick is NOT replaced, and the menu's commands apply to the whole pick or range
The playhead move is instant (same frame as the click, the picture follows at scrub speed) and does not start or stop playback; clicking during playback jumps the playback there
Double click behaviours (a caption's words, opening a title's text) still work

A walk clicks the middle of a clip and checks the playhead time, right-clicks another spot and picks Split Here and checks the cut landed there, and right-clicks inside a two-clip pick and checks the pick is kept
Audit under queue/audits/; anything left rough is filed as a follow-up task if it clears the follow-up bar (queue/bin/follow-up-bar.md), and written into this task's log if it does not.

log.note: Reproduced at Next defaults (/tmp/tl-repro/repro.json, Scripts/playtest.sh --no-build): playhead at 0, windowClick on the middle of Tutorial Sample clip (1107,868), its sound (1107,930), a Title Page bar (400,835), a zoom bar (1107,897), and rightClick on the clip at (1200,868): expectTimeline playheadMS 0 passed after every one. The playhead never moves today.

Adversarial review before building: a Premiere editor expects a clip click to pick only (Premiere moves the playhead on a click only with 'selection follows playhead' habits), but the user asked for Final Cut's skimming-like feel, so that is the spec. Collisions found while building, and decided: (1) a right click on a cut or edit point must NOT move the playhead, or Roll Edit to Playhead could never do anything (roll-the-cut-between-two-clips-walk caught it); (2) a zoom bar's pick puts its framing box up and any playhead move takes it down, so the zoom click moves the playhead first, then picks (a-click-on-the-zoom-bar-frames-it-walk); (3) Start/End at Playhead on a title bar's right-click can now only reach moments inside the bar; the menu bar's Clip > Animate rows still reach any moment. Said in the audit's rough and evaluate.

How it works: SwiftUI's context menus never say where the click landed, so the dock's mouse monitor notes a right press on the tracks (TimelineRightPress, offered by hand from the walk harness the way TimelineKeyRouter is), and every timeline item menu reports what it is about as SwiftUI builds it (measured: the menu body runs inside menu(for:)). Other menus are rebuilt in the same pass (a zoom lane's menu took a press meant for the clip above it), so a menu only counts when the press is on its own row (trackDropRows/zoomLaneRows) and inside its time; that menu moves the playhead before its rows are worked out, and picks its item a turn later unless it is already in the pick. Files: EditorState+TimelinePointing.swift, PhotonzCore/TimelinePointing.swift (+ splitClips), ClipPiecesBar/ZoomLane/CaptionCuesLayer/SoundLane/TimelineTrackRows taps, rightClick step gained 'across'.

Walks: ran all 176 walks that open a recording and click or right-click anything, in batches. Updated 7 that right-clicked a clip somewhere and expected an at-playhead row to act at an earlier playhead (a-zoom-follows-the-cursor, a-zoom-is-shaped-by-hand, drawn-shape-gets-a-timeline-row, ripple-trim-from-the-clip-menu, timeline-right-click, title-bar-right-click-menu, title-flies-in-grows-and-fades-out); all pass. section-fold-motion-walk failed twice at step 36 with this change and once at step 59 without it (it also failed in the 2026-10-12 full sweep), then passed whole with this change: a flaky second press on a section header, not this work.

Rough items: none cleared the follow-up bar as new work. The edit-point exception, the title Start/End at Playhead reach, and multi-pick rows that still act on one clip (Speed, Freeze Frame) are judgement calls left in the audit's evaluate/rough for the user to react to. left rough: a right click on empty track space, a key diamond or a title part's row does not move the playhead (those menus are not about one moment on an item); section-fold-motion-walk is flaky at its second Time-section press (seen 2026-10-12, no task owns it; failed in the last full sweep too, so the standing walk task will pick it up).

Shipped in f197e266 (Next, shared timeline code): a click on a clip, sound, title, caption or zoom bar picks it and moves the playhead to the moment clicked; a right click moves it before the menu is built and picks the item unless already picked; inside a multi-pick, Split/Delete/Ripple Delete act on the whole pick and the pick is kept; cuts and edit points leave the playhead alone (Roll Edit to Playhead). Verified: clicking-a-timeline-item-moves-the-playhead-walk at Next defaults (no flags), 176 recording walks rerun (7 updated to right-click at the moment they mean), Scripts/test.sh 12,800 green, audit queue/audits/2026-10-12-timeline-click-playhead.json.

Its acceptance that a right click moves the playhead is reversed by the user's word of 2026-10-13 (task a-right-click-on-the-timeline-never-moves-the-pl): a right click now only picks. clicking-a-timeline-item-moves-the-playhead-walk was rewritten to park the playhead and check it stays put.
